title: Sprint capacity planning that survives holidays, leave and shared team members
text: Medium Sprint capacity planning that survives holidays, leave and shared team members | by Thofiq Ahmed | Oct, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Step 1 — Start from a calendar, not a number Step 2 — Look at capacity per skill Step 3 — Apply changes in bulk Step 4 — Keep a buffer and say it out loud Step 5 — Share it How I do this Agile Methodology Scrum Master Project Management Product Management Jira Sprint capacity planning that survives holidays, leave and shared team members Thofiq Ahmed 2 min read · Oct 26, 2026 -- Listen Share Stop committing to velocity and start counting real hours “We had the velocity for it” is the most common explanation for a missed sprint. Velocity told you what the team did on an average sprint. It didn’t know that two people were on leave, Thursday was a public holiday in one country, and your only database specialist was spending half her time on another team. Press enter or click to view image in full size Capacity sheet UI Step 1 — Start from a calendar, not a number Build a simple grid: team members as rows, working days as columns, default hours in each cell (for example 8h). Then mark what’s different: Weekends and public holidays per member’s country — distributed teams don’t share holidays. Planned leave and half days. Part-time and shared members: if someone works for two teams, give this team only its share (for example 4h/day) for the whole sprint. The sum is your real capacity in hours. Compare it with the average; the difference is the risk you were about to commit to. Step 2 — Look at capacity per skill Total hours hide bottlenecks. Tag each member with skills (backend, frontend, QA, data…) and total the hours per skill. A sprint with 300 hours but only 20 QA hours will not ship 300 hours of testable work. Step 3 — Apply changes in bulk Capacity changes often apply to many cells at once: a team offsite, a shared member’s recurring split, a regional holiday. Doing these cell by cell is where mistakes creep in. Apply them to everyone or to selected people over a date range, and make sure resetting a day back to normal is as easy as changing it. Step 4 — Keep a buffer and say it out loud Commit to around 70–80% of real capacity. Meetings, reviews, support and surprises are real work. Write the buffer into the plan instead of hoping for it. Step 5 — Share it Capacity is a conversation with the Product Owner and stakeholders, so export it (an Excel file is still the universal format) and attach it to the sprint plan. How I do this Disclosure: I’m the maker of PreJira. In PreJira the capacity sheet is part of sprint planning: holidays per country, per-day statuses like leave or half day, bulk apply for everyone or selected members, totals per skill, and an Excel (.xlsx) export.
